synthesis: scout:record-check-ins matches each Scout kit's GPS (clarity.sc_positions) against its org's open Direct/Staging order addresses and persists one row per (kit, address, hour) into platform.scout_check_ins. It exhausted a production host's memory on 2026-08-12 (~29GB marginal across a measured peak of 17 concurrent processes, ~30GB headroom) and forced a reboot; the schedule has been commented out since commit 11bc23e2 and stays disabled until the ACs are met. PR #323 shipped observability-only and is NOT the fix; this is a fresh restart. Root cause is a chain, not a single bug: (1) every sc_positions read wraps kit_mapping in lower(), disabling the table's case-sensitive (kit_mapping, timestamp_utc) primary key (3056/32732 granules vs 13/32732 exact-case), inflating cycle duration; (2) the largest org has ~255k open-order addresses; (3) the amplifier: the recorder pulls that whole address list OUT of ClickHouse into a PHP array (ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery), re-serializes it as an inline SQL values() literal, and pushes it BACK in 2000-row chunks per kit (ScoutCheckInMatchQuery, ~5,500 CH queries/cycle) -- both the duration and the memory driver; (4) withoutOverlapping(10) is a lock EXPIRY, not a duration cap, so 36-209min cycles let a new process start ~every 10min, driving concurrency to ~17-21 with no ceiling; (5) each process holds its own O(addresses_per_org) copy ($addresses across the 43-kit loop, array_chunk() copying the whole array per kit, $matches[] accumulating) -> total host memory O(addresses x concurrency), unbounded. Intended outcome (this PR = W2+W3): compute the match server-side in ONE ClickHouse statement per unit of work by lifting ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's matches CTE (the DEV-1758 extension point its own docblock names) onto sc_positions, so only ~40 match rows/cycle cross into PHP; add a hard concurrency ceiling that holds independent of runtime; add the missing peak-memory regression test (AC6), fix the AC7 silent-failure gap (ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows Throwable to [] in prod so a failed match looks identical to an empty one), and add a parity check vs ScoutCheckInRollupQuery on the shared domain rule (AC9). W1 (the chlocal-owned sc_positions lower(kit_mapping) projection that makes the CH side itself fast) is out of scope -- platform is SELECT-only. W4 (re-enabling the schedule + production host verification) is an operational, prod-only step gated on production observation, not a code change this PR can complete or prove.

scope.summary: Rewrite the two-query recorder path (ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery + ScoutCheckInMatchQuery, orchestrated by ScoutRecordCheckIns) so ClickHouse computes the (kit, address, hour) match server-side in one statement per org/kit and returns only matches -- never an address list -- eliminating the PHP round-trip amplifier (AC1). Lift ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's CTE (open_hotlists -> address_links -> addresses, bbox-prefiltered, geoDistance <= 160.934m) adapted from clarity.scans_{hot,cold}+org_id/kit_id onto clarity.sc_positions+lower(kit_mapping). Add a hard, runtime-independent concurrency ceiling (W3, AC4). Fix the silent-failure gap so a failed CH read is distinguishable from a legitimately empty one (AC7). Add a peak-memory regression test at prod-representative cardinality (AC6) and a parity test vs ScoutCheckInRollupQuery (AC9). Keep BOTH prunes on public_address, the bbox pad, extract()+toFloat64OrNull EWKT parsing (never readWKTPoint), and no FINAL on the two zod CDC tables. Do NOT touch the sc_positions schema (W1, chlocal-owned) and do NOT re-enable the schedule (W4, operational/prod-only). Keep the pass to W2+W3+AC6/AC7/AC9; do not resurrect the cap/watermark/planner machinery already tried and descoped twice on this ticket.

proposed_changes.change: Replace the values()-injection + array_chunk architecture with a single self-contained CTE per call: position_window (clarity.sc_positions, lower(kit_mapping) [= or IN -- Q1/Q4], time window) -> bbox prefilter (same BBOX_PAD_DEGREES=0.003 as the rollup) -> open_hotlists (clarity.hotlist FINAL, status=Open, length(plate)>3, org/staging filter) -> address_links (zod.public_hotlist_address, DISTINCT/_peerdb_is_deleted=0, is_staged) -> addresses (zod.public_address, id IN (subquery) prune KEPT alongside the address_links JOIN, extract()+toFloat64OrNull EWKT parse, no FINAL) -> geoDistance <= 160.934 join -> GROUP BY (address_id, hour_bucket) with the existing argMin/min direct-preference tie-break (keep the outer SELECT's argMin(hotlist_id,(toUInt8(is_staged),hotlist_id))/min(is_staged) verbatim). Prefer self::zodDb() over hardcoding 'zod.' (matching ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery, not the rollup's hardcode). Remove addresses param, addressValues(), ADDRESS_CHUNK. Returns only match rows (~40/cycle). NOTE: candidate-0's alternative is a NEW sibling class (e.g. ScoutCheckInGpsMatchQuery) + retire this one for discoverability -- a minor naming/placement choice, not gate-material.
proposed_changes.reason: AC1 -- the ticket's designated 'architecture to lift' (the docblock's DEV-1758 lift point); direct fix for the PHP<->CH round-trip amplifier and the primary duration/memory driver.

proposed_changes.change: Drop openOrderAddressesForOrg()/the per-org address cache and the $addresses threading through recordCheckInsForKit(); call the rewritten matcher once per unit of work (per-org or per-kit -- Q4) and replace the per-match firstOrCreate() loop with one bulk ScoutCheckIn::query()->insertOrIgnore($rows) against the existing unique(kit_id,address_id,hour_bucket) (insertOrIgnore returns the inserted-row count, so $recorded accounting still works, but created_at/updated_at must be stamped manually since it bypasses model events). Add the W3 concurrency ceiling at command start (exit early / no-op if no slot, or per-org queued dispatch). For AC7, bypass ClickhouseQuery::query()'s Throwable-swallow at the failure-sensitive call sites (majority lean: call ::handle() directly, replicating any residual caching via an explicit Cache::remember() at the call site) so the command's EXISTING per-org/per-kit try/catch blocks actually receive a thrown exception in production. Keep the completion-summary/overrun logging.
proposed_changes.reason: AC1/AC3/AC4/AC7 -- removes the amplifier and the accumulator, bounds concurrency, and makes the dead-code failure guard live.

questions.q: IN vs equality on lower(kit_mapping) for the new server-side matcher: one statement per ORG (lower(kit_mapping) IN (...), which the optimizer may ignore and lose the sc_positions prefix prune, ~12 queries/cycle) vs one per KIT (equality, prunes cleanly but ~43 queries/cycle)? evidence-38238 says settle with EXPLAIN and prefer more queries over losing the prune; note that on the CURRENT unprojected table (pre-W1) BOTH shapes are slow, so this also affects whether W2 alone suffices before W1.
questions.answer: DECIDE BY EXPLAIN FIRST: run a read-only Cloud EXPLAIN (clarity_clickhouse is Cloud-connected, read-only) on BOTH per-kit equality and per-org IN early in implementation; adopt whichever actually prunes the sc_positions prefix, preferring the prune over query count per evidence-38238. Batching granularity (Q index 3) follows from this same decision.

questions.q: Does ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's bbox-prefilter performance profile -- tuned against LPR scans -- actually transfer to clarity.sc_positions, whose GPS fixes arrive ~every 3s so position_window is far larger and the bbox far less selective? The brief flags this as unmeasured, not assumed-safe; it may need its own tuning (e.g. GPS decimation before the bbox, per PG-022).
questions.answer: VALIDATE VIA THE SAME EXPLAIN/query_log step: measure position_window size + read_rows for a real dense kit over a 15-min window. Add GPS decimation (e.g. one fix per N seconds via toStartOfInterval) inside position_window ONLY if the window proves too large/unselective. Do not pre-optimize.

questions.q: W3 concurrency-ceiling mechanism: an N-slot Cache::lock semaphore acquired at command start (no Cache::lock precedent anywhere in app/) vs per-org queued jobs (Horizon). A working per-org prototype exists in git history -- App\Jobs\Scout\RecordOrgCheckIns at commit caab5a469, reverted at 102a3430 only because {low}-supervisor maxProcesses defaults to 1 and serialized throughput ~7x at the OLD ~104-min per-org duration. W2 collapses per-org duration to one CH statement, changing the throughput math the DEV-2347 revert was based on -- re-evaluate, do not re-assume the old conclusion. Coupling invariant (DEV-2348): if lock expiry rises, lookback must be >= it (today 10 < 15).
questions.answer: DEFER TO THE PHASE 3 PLAN: the single-arbiter plan chooses the mechanism (N-slot Cache::lock semaphore vs per-org queued jobs / revived RecordOrgCheckIns), informed by the chosen W2 shape. It MUST satisfy AC4 (a hard ceiling that holds independent of runtime) and preserve the DEV-2348 coupling invariant (lock expiry <= lookback; today 10 < 15). The discredited 'concurrency is load-bearing' reasoning must NOT inform the choice.

questions.q: Batching granularity for W2: per-org (fewer, larger queries; couples to the IN-vs-equality prune risk above; maps naturally onto a per-org job) or per-kit (more, smaller, individually prunable queries; does not map onto per-org jobs)?
questions.answer: FOLLOWS FROM THE W2 SHAPE (EXPLAIN-driven, Q index 0): per-org batching iff per-org IN prunes acceptably, else per-kit. Whichever is chosen must keep per-statement memory O(matches).

questions.q: How do AC2 (full-cycle duration < 5-min cadence, measured) and AC3 (peak RSS x plausible concurrency fits ~30GB, measured) get verified when this pipeline has no production or prod-scale-staging access and a local Docker CH cannot hold 255k real addresses at realistic geo-distribution? Only a read-only Cloud EXPLAIN/query_log session (as evidence-38238 prescribes for W1) appears available, and that does not cover the command's wall-clock.
questions.answer: EXPLAIN NOW, WALL-CLOCK AT W4: prove the query PLAN via read-only Cloud EXPLAIN/query_log (AC5-style evidence for the platform side) + a local peak-RSS regression test at representative cardinality (AC6) + the structural O(matches) memory argument. AC2 (full-cycle duration) + AC3 (host memory fit) + AC8 (host pct_usable) are GATED ON THE W4 SUPERVISED RE-ENABLE with a Datadog memory watch -- explicitly NOT verified in CI. This PR ships W2+W3+tests; prod-scale duration/memory is verified at re-enable.

Do not cite either as support for any W3 design choice.

Git history: DEV-2342 was worked through several iterations before this fresh restart (b25a6fe6 -> 55e1bbcc -> f34a5cda -> caab5a46 -> 102a3430 -> 11bc23e2), including trying and reverting a DEV-2347 per-org job dispatcher (App\Jobs\Scout\RecordOrgCheckIns, caab5a469, deleted 102a3430) and a 90-then-20-minute lock-expiry change. The reverts happened because the OLD (pre-W2) per-cycle duration made them net-negative; W2 changes that math -- re-derive the tradeoffs, do not assume the old conclusions still hold.

A prior 'advance-on-clean-pass watermark' attempt at AC7 was built and reverted (commit 2cd844090) specifically because ClickhouseQuery::query()'s in-production Throwable-swallow made the guard unreachable -- proven by a failing test. Any AC7 fix must not rely on catching an exception thrown out of ::query(); it must go through ::handle() directly or another signal entirely.

ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows \Throwable to [] only in production|testing; in local/other envs it re-throws. Every existing failure-mode test exploits this by flipping app.env to 'local' -- an AC7 test must instead reach the production swallow path to prove the fix.

config/scout.php's own docblock states its no-fallback discipline exists specifically because 'DEV-2342 shipped one knob with three different defaults' -- any new W3 tunable must follow the identical pattern (config is the single source of truth, no call-site fallback).

PG-022 precedent (okf/concepts/platform-gotchas.md): for continuous-GPS work the memory cost is almost always PHP not ClickHouse, and the established fix is to move per-point cost into CH and return a pre-reduced result (KitRangePathsQuery: O(segments) not O(points), ~1GB refused -> ~20MB proven). W2 is the same template applied to check-in matching (O(matches) not O(addresses)) -- second application of an established pattern, not a novel design.

insertOrIgnore() returns an int count of rows actually inserted -- a drop-in replacement for the current wasRecentlyCreated-based $recorded increment -- and relies on the SAME existing unique(kit_id,address_id,hour_bucket) index, so no migration is needed. BUT it bypasses model events, so created_at/updated_at must be stamped manually in the bulk rows.

No command or job anywhere in app/ uses Cache::lock() or the WithoutOverlapping job middleware (confirmed by grep) -- W3 has no in-repo sibling pattern to copy; whichever mechanism is chosen is a first for this repo (though both are standard Laravel).

Structural difference when adapting the CTE: ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's LHS is clarity.scans_{hot,cold} FINAL WHERE org_id=? AND kit_id=? (integer keys); sc_positions has NO org_id/kit_id column -- it is ORDER BY (kit_mapping, timestamp_utc), string-keyed, and every reader wraps both sides in lower() (DEV-2012). This is not a drop-in table swap.

Binding hazards to preserve verbatim when lifting the rollup CTE (its own docblock): keep BBOX_PAD_DEGREES (0.003 deg) prefiltering addresses before the geoDistance join; keep BOTH the id IN (subquery) prune on zod.public_address AND the INNER JOIN to address_links (dropping either full-scans the 196M-row table or loses is_staged); parse EWKT with extract()+toFloat64OrNull, never readWKTPoint (throws on a malformed row, which ClickhouseQuery then silently empties); skip FINAL on the two zod CDC tables, relying on _peerdb_is_deleted=0 + DISTINCT.

ScoutCheckInRollupQuery hardcodes the 'zod.' database prefix literally instead of using self::zodDb() (a known ~15-class local-CH-QA limitation) -- prefer the dynamic self::zodDb() pattern (matching ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery, which this rewrite absorbs) in the new code.

resource_envelope.allocation_sketch: CURRENT (the incident): per-process PHP memory is O(addresses_per_org) -- the full org address array held across the 43-kit loop, array_chunk() copying the whole array per kit (~128 chunks for the largest org), plus $matches[] accumulating with no streaming -- multiplied by UNBOUNDED concurrency (measured peak 17, driven by withoutOverlapping(10)'s expiry-not-cap semantics against 36-209min cycles). Measured ~1.5-3 GB/process x ~17 processes = ~29 GB marginal against ~30 GB host headroom = the outage. So total host memory is O(addresses_per_org x concurrency), both terms large. PROPOSED (W2+W3): per-process memory O(matches_per_cycle) -- only ~40 rows/cycle ever reach PHP regardless of the underlying address-set size (whether an org has 3 open addresses or the measured 296,459 on a single hotlist), because enumeration + the geoDistance join both happen inside the single ClickHouse statement; combined with W3's hard ceiling, worst-case host memory becomes N_slots x O(matches) -- small, bounded, and roughly constant instead of scaling with org address-book size and unbounded concurrency.
